Beállítom Mihajlo Fedorov volt ukrán védelmi miniszter kedden közzétett egy videót, amiben többek között arról is beszél, hogy Ukrajnának meg kell teremtenie a demokráciát a háború alatt is, azaz annak a feltételeit, hogy az ország akár választásokat tudjon tartani. Volodimir Zelenszkij ukrán elnök július közepén menesztette Fedorovot . A népszerű, 35 éves Fedorov leváltása országos, több ezer ember részvételével zajló tiltakozáshullámot indított el Ukrajnában . Fedorov miniszteri székét Jevhen Hmara, az Ukrán Nemzetbiztonsági Szolgálat (SZBU) ideiglenes vezetője kapta meg, akit augusztus 19-én fognak beiktatni. Fedorov a keddi videójában arról beszél, hogy szükség van egy „legális, biztonságos és reális” választási folyamatra, amivel le tudják adni a voksaikat a hadsereg tagjai, a külföldön élő ukránok, és azok is, akik a front közelében laknak. A volt miniszter szerint nem szabad megengedni, hogy Putyin döntse el, mikor választhatja meg Ukrajna a kormányát. Szerinte a demokrácia nem luxust, a demokrácia az, amiért Ukrajna a mai napig harcol. Fedorov a videóban kritizálta a háborús helyzet alatti felesleges bürokráciát, és a jelenlegi kormányt is, amiért nem kommunikál megfelelően a lakossággal. Arról is beszélt, hogy a választás nem csak a voksokról szól, hanem arról a lehetőségről, ami az állampolgároknak megadatik, hogy értékeljék a hatalmon lévőket, és eldöntsék, jár-e nekik a bizalom. Az 1991-es születésű Fedorov 2019-ben Zelenszkij elnökválasztási kampányának digitális felelőse volt, majd az új kormány legfiatalabb tagjaként azonnal kormányfőhelyettes lett, és megkapta a digitális átalakításért felelős minisztérium vezetését is. Négy évvel később oktatási, tudományos és technológiai fejlesztésért felelős miniszter lett, majd két évvel később visszatért a digitális tárca élére, ahonnan 2026 elején a védelmi miniszter székébe ült át. A Kyiv Independent szerint Fedorov visszautasította Zelenszkij ajánlatait a többi tárcára, mondván hogy csak a védelmi miniszteri pozíciót fogadná el a felmentése után. How severe is Germany's 2026 harvest decline? The German Farmers' Association (DBV) on Tuesday warned of a "below-average" harvest due to ongoing drought that has left large areas of farmland severely parched. In a statement, DBV President Joachim Rukwied warned that the country's grain harvest would be 7% lower than last year, blaming an "overly dry spring and a heat wave in the second half of June," which had "significantly damaged many crops." Overall grain production was expected to be 41.9 million tons this year, the DBV said, a shortfall of some 3.3 million tons compared with 2025. Rapeseed saw the largest fall, with 3.3 million tons harvested, nearly 17% lower than last year. Barley remained at last year's level despite a lower yield, as more land was used to grow the crop. The potato crop was also expected to be below average and some regions would see a "significantly worse" harvest for sugar beet, DBV said. Rukwied noted how location played a bigger role in determining crop yields this year than usual, and pointed to poor crop yields and even crop failures, particularly in southern and western Germany. German farmers face harvest losses, price uncertainty To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Separately, Germany's Federal Statistical Office warned that the country's apple harvest was forecast to drop 18% compared with last year. Germany is experiencing a severe drought during a summer of frequent record-breaking temperatures , which has exacerbated the effects of below-average rainfall since March, according to the German Weather Service. 2. How will the drought affect food prices and availability? Agriculture Minister Alois Rainer told public broadcaster ZDF on Tuesday that ministers "don't expect prices to rise immediately," leaving open the possibility of a time lag before consumers pay more for groceries. However, Philipp Spinne, managing director of the German Raiffeisen Association (DRV), which represents 1,600 agricultural cooperatives, told DW its members had already suffered "pure losses in the field" of €600 million ($696 million). "At the moment, many areas of farming and the chain are not covering their costs," Spinne warned, describing how higher fertilizer, energy and logistics costs were adding to the pressure on farmers. In Germany, some fields have suffered total or near-total crop failure due to drought and excessive heat Image: Frank Hoermann/SvenSimon/picture alliance Germany does have a 2 million-ton grain surplus from last year's harvest, according to government data, which could prevent a hike in bread prices. Yet, the sharp drop in rapeseed and sugar beet production may strain domestic oil and sugar supplies, requiring imports to make up the shortfall. Local media reported last week that the drought had also caused a drastic fall in animal feed stocks in several states, particularly in southern Germany. The German Farmers' Association warned of a reduction in livestock numbers, due to “major challenges” in feed supply. This could push up prices for meat, milk and eggs. In the hardest-hit areas of the country, potatoes and other vegetables could become more expensive as supply tightens. For most shoppers, however, the main impact is more likely to be gradual price increases rather than shortages. 3. How does this drought fit into wider food security concerns? Farming, both at home and globally, has faced repeated pressures since the COVID-19 pandemic. German food prices have risen by over 36% since 2020, according to government data published last month. The price hikes were especially strong for poultry meat, many dairy products and eggs, edible fats and oils, and sugar, the government calculated. Russia's war in Ukraine disrupted Black Sea exports of Ukrainian grain in 2022 and drove energy prices higher, impacting the cost of fertilizer, transport and food processing. More recently, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz due to the Iran war prevented oil, gas and fertilizer ingredients from leaving the Gulf. The conflict has pushed up prices of diesel fuel, fertilizers and pesticides , with some farmers cutting back on soil nutrients. Compounding crises over the past six years have left large parts of the German agriculture sector financially stretched, the industry has warned. Many farmers have said they face much higher costs and rising debts, and have limited room to absorb further losses. In previous years, farmers have used tractors to blockade roads to pressure the government for help Image: Daniel Bockwoldt/dpa/picture alliance 4. What support are German farmers seeking? The German Farmers' Association said some farmers may need interim financing to secure their futures. Rukwied called on Berlin to launch an "immediate package" to help support the agriculture sector. Recommendations include boosting the European Union's fertilizer aid package from €60 million to €180 million, paid out quickly and without red tape. DBV also called on ministers to cut the tax on agricultural diesel, at least until the end of November. For several months from late 2023, German farmers blocked highways with tractors over plans to scrap fuel subsidies for the agricultural sector, which were later partially reversed. Agriculture Minister Rainer promised targeted help to farmers, but only when reliable official figures are available at the end of August. Bishops Around the World Ask for Prayers for Pope Leo XIV’s Health Prayers for the Pope’s health have been pouring in from all over the world. Pope Leo XIV pictured on Oct. 1, 2026, praying a Rosary for peace with hundreds of children in the Vatican Gardens. Bishops around the world are calling for prayers upon his announcement that he will undergo a medical procedure this week to remove a nodule on his lung. (Photo: Daniel Ibáñez/EWTN News / Vatican Pool ) Diego López Marina/EWTN News/ACI Prensa Nation October 11, 2026 Bishops from around the world asked for prayers for Pope Leo XIV after he announced on Sunday, Oct. 11, that he will undergo surgery to remove a nodule on one of his lungs in the coming days. In the United States, Archbishop Paul Coakley, president of the U.S. bishops’ conference, said the prelates would join “the faithful and all people of good will in praying for his good health.” He also prayed for those who will perform the operation: “May the hand of Pope Leo’s surgeons be guided by the divine physician, Jesus Christ.” Archbishop Ronald Hicks of New York joined the prayers as he finished a week-long pilgrimage on the Camino de Santiago in Spain. “I join with the bishops, priests, faithful, and all people of good will of the Archdiocese of New York in praying for our Holy Father, Pope Leo XIV, as he prepares for his surgery later this week,” he wrote . He also asked Jesus, “the divine physician,” to care for the Pope and guide “the hands of his surgeons, nurses, and other health professionals.” Prayers from Uruguay, Argentina, and Peru Cardinal Daniel Sturla, archbishop of Montevideo, also wrote about the news. Uruguay is one of the countries expecting Pope Leo XIV on his upcoming visit to Latin America. “Let us pray for his speedy recovery and continue with greater spirit the preparation for his visit to our land,” he wrote. In Peru, which also expects the Pope later this year, the Archdiocese of Lima entrusted his health to the Lord of Miracles, a devotion that draws millions of Peruvians each year. “We ask the Lord of Miracles for his speedy recovery,” the archdiocese said on social media. The Peruvian bishops’ conference issued a message titled “United in prayer for the health of the Holy Father Leo XIV.” It noted the “serenity and humility” with which the Pope shared the news and asked that his health be entrusted to the Lord of Miracles. “Lifting to God, Lord of life and source of all health, our supplications that he strengthen him and grant him the health that the fulfillment of his mission requires,” the Peruvian bishops said. They also urged communities, families, and the faithful to place the Holy Father under the maternal protection of the Blessed Virgin Mary, so that in the fullness of his strength he may continue his mission in service of the Church and all humanity, as a messenger of peace and hope and a witness of unity, fraternity, and encounter among all peoples. The Argentinian bishops said in a statement: “We ask the Lord to grant him strength and peace at this time, that the operation may go well, and that he may make a swift and full recovery.” Prayers from Spain The Spanish bishops’ conference also invited prayer for the Pope. Its president, Archbishop Luis Argüello, asked “the whole Spanish Church — dioceses, institutes of consecrated life, communities and lay associations, all members of the People of God, and our fellow citizens — to pray for the health of our beloved Pope Leo XIV.” The conference’s secretary general, Bishop Francisco César García Magán, recalled the welcome Leo XIV received on his recent visit to Spain and said the faithful can now show him their closeness in another way: “Now we show it by uniting in prayer.” The conference’s secretary general, Bishop Francisco César García Magán, recalled the welcome Leo XIV received on his recent visit to Spain and said the faithful can now show him their closeness in another way: “Now we show it by uniting in prayer.” Prayers from Poland, Great Britain, Malta Archbishop Tadeusz Wojda, the president of the Polish Bishops’ Conference, issued an appeal to the Polish people, asking them to “pray for the Holy Father, Pope Leo XIV, asking God for a successful operation and a speedy recovery.” Bishop John Keenan, on behalf of the Scottish bishops’ conference, said : “We invite Catholics across Scotland, and all people of goodwill, to join us in praying for Pope Leo, for the medical team caring for him, and for a successful operation and a full and speedy recovery.” Archbishop Richard Moth of Westminster and the president of the Catholic Bishops’ Conference of England and Wales, assured Leo of the prayers of the faithful. “We pray that following the procedure and a period of recovery, he will soon be restored to health,” Archbishop Moth wrote. Archbishop Charles Scicluna, Archbishop of Malta and Adjunct Secretary of the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, wrote on X : “The Church in Malta is united in prayer for the Holy Father, wishing him well for the surgery he will be undergoing.” Leo XIV Asks for Prayers The Pope announced the operation after Sunday’s Angelus. Doctors found a nodule on one of his lungs and recommended removing it.
